statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 24: direct U.S.-Iran military escalation and constrained Hormuz shipping keep Sunday reopening-gap sensitivity elevated, while the weekend NQ closure provides no live evidence of persistent one-way Nasdaq structure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme from the direct U.S.-Iran exchange, constrained Gulf shipping, energy inflation pressure and Friday's higher-rate repricing. The Sunday futures reopening remains the next live price-path checkpoint.
headline: U.S.-Iran tanker escalation keeps closed-market Nasdaq regime at WATCH
body: NQ is closed for the weekend. U.S. Central Command confirmed strikes on three Iranian crude carriers after Iranian missile attacks on two U.S. Navy ships. Hormuz shipping remains well below its recent average, while Friday's strong jobs report pushed yields higher and left the Nasdaq lower. No live NQ price path is available during the closure.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours show Friday's post-jobs live-trading risk normalizing after a late orange episode, followed by low Tail during the weekend closure and a shift back to WATCH after the confirmed U.S.-Iran tanker and naval exchange. Since the close, Tail reflects discontinuity and reopening risk rather than observed mean-reversion failure.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed through all 24 forecast slots. If no additional verified U.S.-Iran or Hormuz escalation occurs, Tail is projected to ease within WATCH before edging modestly higher as Sunday reopening approaches; Stress remains extreme from conflict, energy and rate pressure. The reopening after this horizon is the next live price-path test.
